name: Tychicus
title: Paul's Faithful Messenger
summary: Tychicus was a faithful coworker and messenger for the apostle Paul. He came from the province of Asia and served as an envoy who delivered several of Paul's letters to the churches. Paul described him as a beloved brother, a faithful servant, and a fellow worker in the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Traveling with Paul to Asia
keyEvents.description: Tychicus from the province of Asia was among those who accompanied Paul on his return journey through Macedonia, as part of a group of coworkers from various churches.

keyEvents.title: Messenger to Ephesus
keyEvents.description: Paul sent Tychicus to the church in Ephesus with his letter, to inform them about how Paul was doing and to encourage their hearts.

keyEvents.title: Messenger to Colossae
keyEvents.description: Tychicus was sent together with Onesimus to Colossae with Paul's letter, to inform the church about Paul's situation and comfort them.

keyEvents.title: Possible Mission to Crete
keyEvents.description: Paul considered sending either Artemas or Tychicus to Titus in Crete, so that Titus could travel on to Paul in Nicopolis.

keyEvents.title: Sent to Ephesus during Paul's Second Imprisonment
keyEvents.description: During his second imprisonment in Rome, Paul sent Tychicus to Ephesus, possibly to relieve Timothy so that Timothy could come to Paul.
